source.title: After the Default
source.summary: Debt jubilees, odious debt, and whether Islamic principles offer a reset for over-indebted nations.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: What happens when a nation simply cannot pay? Argentina has defaulted nine times. Lebanon's debt-to-GDP hit 150% before its economy collapsed. Sri Lanka defaulted in 2022 after running out of foreign reserves. The modern system offers few options: austerity, restructuring, or collapse. But Islamic tradition has a different concept. The Quran explicitly encourages creditors to forgive debts when debtors face hardship. The concept of odious debt, that populations shouldn't repay loans taken by dictators against their interests, resonates deeply with Islamic principles of justice. This final episode examines historical and modern debt crises, the growing movement for debt jubilees and cancellation, and proposes an Islamic framework for sovereign debt resolution that prioritizes human welfare over creditor returns.
